text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Frederick Chiluba on Monday announced a new cabinet in which he has re-appointed most of his old ministers, brought in five new faces and created a cabinet portfolio at State House.

- Nine Britons aboard a South African Airways plane were over the weekend sent back to Johannesburg after they arrived in Lusaka without entry visas. Zambia introduced visa requirements for Britons last month after Britain introduced a similar requirement for Zambians.
- Norway is pleased with Zambia for maintaining an open dialogue policy with donors, Norwegian ambassador designate Jon Lemoey said on Monday.

- The current level of grain storage in the Southern African Development Community (SADC) indicates a lack of regional co-operation, programme manager at the SADC centre in Harare, Lovemore Mafurirano told an economic workshop in Lusaka.
